key_themes: AI infrastructure rally led by CoreWeave earnings beat
Semiconductor and memory stock surge (Micron, Sandisk, Nvidia rebound)
Photonics stocks soar on AI connectivity demand (Coherent, Lumentum)

stocks.discussion_driver: CoreWeave surged ~25% after Q3 earnings beat — the company lost only $1.27/share on $3.66B revenue (better than feared) and raised its full-year revenue outlook. As a major AI infrastructure provider and NVIDIA's largest cloud customer, the strong results reignited the broader AI trade across the market.
bull_case: AI infrastructure demand is accelerating with no signs of slowdown, and CoreWeave is uniquely positioned as a pure-play cloud provider for GPU-intensive workloads
Revenue beat and raised full-year guidance demonstrate strong execution and growing hyperscaler customer commitments
bear_case: Company remains deeply unprofitable with high capital expenditure requirements to build and maintain AI data center infrastructure
Stock was recently downgraded by Stifel (target cut to $60 from $120, Hold) reflecting concerns about valuation and profitability timeline

stocks.discussion_driver: Nvidia rebounded 2.87% on November 11 as CoreWeave's strong Q3 results reignited the AI trade narrative and validated ongoing GPU demand. The stock had been under pressure after Baird downgraded it to Neutral with a price target slashed from $500 to $200. Q3 earnings on November 17 will be the next major catalyst.
bull_case: Blackwell GPU architecture is ramping strongly and AI data center demand from hyperscalers remains extremely robust, as evidenced by CoreWeave's raised guidance
Trading at ~22x trailing earnings — cheap for a dominant platform company with AI-driven secular growth tailwinds
bear_case: Baird downgrade to Neutral (PT cut from $500 to $200) reflects growing concerns about whether hyperscaler AI capex spending is sustainable at current levels
Stock is down ~28.6% from 52-week high, suggesting market skepticism is building ahead of the November 17 earnings report

stocks.discussion_driver: SanDisk jumped ~16.5% to close above $1,000 on November 11, riding the AI-driven memory sector rally ignited by CoreWeave's earnings beat. The company also recently announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective November 20, 2026, further boosting investor sentiment. Memory stocks surged broadly on the thesis that AI chip demand will drive sustained NAND flash consumption.
bull_case: AI-driven demand for NAND flash memory and high-bandwidth storage is a multi-year structural tailwind with no near-term supply glut
8-for-1 stock split on November 20 increases retail accessibility; stock trades at a low 7.1x trailing P/E with a $2,056 analyst consensus target
bear_case: Stock remains 57.5% below its 52-week high of $2,354, suggesting the market sees significant headwinds or prior rally was overdone
Memory markets are inherently cyclical; rapid NAND pricing deterioration has historically punished storage stocks when demand softens

stocks.discussion_driver: Micron surged ~13.6% on November 11, rallying in sympathy with SanDisk and the broader AI memory sector following CoreWeave's earnings beat. The stock had been in a steep correction (down ~34% from 52-week highs), but analyst consensus remains strongly bullish with a $1,562 average price target, underpinned by high-bandwidth memory demand for AI training.
bull_case: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) demand for AI model training is a multi-year growth driver and Micron is one of only three HBM suppliers globally
Stock trades at approximately 10.9x trailing earnings with overwhelming analyst support (45 Buy/Strong Buy ratings) and $1,562 average price target implying 90% upside
bear_case: DRAM and NAND markets are historically cyclical; any slowdown in AI capex or memory oversupply could quickly erode pricing and margins
RSI was 35.82 (near oversold) before the Nov 11 bounce, reflecting persistent negative momentum with stock still 34.3% below 52-week high

stocks.discussion_driver: Coherent jumped ~9.2% on November 11 as the AI data-center photonics demand thesis was validated by CoreWeave's earnings beat and raised guidance. The company had reported fiscal Q1 results the week prior and guided for 60%+ revenue growth with its first $4B quarterly revenue by FY2028. After a sharp post-earnings selloff, the stock is now recovering strongly.
bull_case: AI data center optical interconnects and transceivers are a structural multi-year growth market, and Coherent is a leading supplier to hyperscalers
Company guided for 60%+ revenue growth through FY2028 with its first $4B quarter, and Citigroup raised its price target to $440 on November 6
bear_case: Stock trades at 34.8x trailing P/E and remains 46.7% below its 52-week high of $440, with Morgan Stanley maintaining Equal Weight at a reduced $325 target
Multiple analyst firms have recently trimmed price targets (Rosenblatt cut from $500 to $400, Morgan Stanley from $375 to $325), reflecting near-term execution concerns
